question: What if a fart was your only rocket in space?
answer_in_one_line: It would move you one hair's width a minute, so ten feet would take over three weeks; one thrown slipper pushes six thousand times harder and gets you home in five minutes, and in a real, airtight spacesuit the fart never leaves at all.

trend_basis.evidence: fart-rocket-in-space: 'What if You Fart in Space' 57M and 'Fart In A Space Suit' 25M (giant channels); 'If You Fart in a Silent Elevator' 3.4M on an 18.7k-subscriber channel this week.

No fresh everyday 'what if you' row today. Of the 60 rows about 25 are 'Comment ... if you need one' product adverts (the top two at 46.0M and 24.0M views/day), the next group is GTA 6 and film or game what-ifs ('What Happens If You Reach the N in GTA 6?' 2.33M/day, 'What If Star-Lord Never Punched Thanos?' 1.03M/day), and the one physical scenario near the top, 'What Would Happen If You Jumped Through a Hole in the Earth' (16.4k-subscriber channel, 2.58M views/day, and a 2,970-subscriber copy at 0.66M/day), is this channel's first episode.

The last two episodes were a plane story (lightning, 721 views/day on its first day) and a five-seconds story (friction, 799 views/day); both clusters rest today. Personal-survival-in-space is the one kind of space story that works for small channels.
Nothing to cross with: searches and Wikipedia are GTA 6, films and people; the science headlines carry no everyday scenario.

why_this_one: The trend file has no row that passes the four tests, so the topic comes from the bank: the first tier A entry outside the clusters of the last two episodes (plane, five seconds). Everybody has wondered what you could push on if you were stuck floating; the title is plain nouns a ten-year-old laughs at; and the answer is a surprise that numbers carry: one hair's width a minute, three weeks for ten feet, and one slipper worth six thousand farts. The ending is real physics too: a spacesuit is airtight, so the gas never leaves and the push is exactly zero. It is drawable with flat cards in empty space, the kit garden and a road; nobody is hurt and there is nothing to imitate.
